Module 1.title: Wave Optics: Interference and Diffraction of Light
Module 1.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Wave Optics
  • Interference in Thin Films: Cosine law $2 \mu t \cos r = n \lambda$ (constructive in transmitted, destructive in reflected with Stokes $\pi$ phase shift: $2 \mu t \cos r = (2n-1)\frac{\lambda}{2}$).
  • Newton's Rings: Diameter of $n$-th dark ring: $D_n = \sqrt{4 n R \lambda}$. $\lambda = \frac{D_{n+p}^2 - D_n^2}{4 p R}$.
  • Fraunhofer Diffraction (Single Slit): Minima condition: $a \sin \theta = m \lambda$ ($m = \pm 1, \pm 2$). Central maximum width: $2 \lambda / a$.
  • Diffraction Grating: Grating equation $(a + b) \sin \theta = n \lambda$. Resolving power $\frac{\lambda}{d\lambda} = n N$.
Module 1.detailed_notes:
Module 1 Reference: Optics

Rayleigh criterion for resolution: Two spectral lines are barely resolved when the central diffraction maximum of one coincides with the first minimum of the other.
Module 1.textbook_html:
1.1 Physical Wave Optics & Optical Metrology

Module 2.title: Quantum Mechanics and Nanophysics
Module 2.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Quantum Mechanics
  • De Broglie Wavelength: $\lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{h}{m v} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m E}}$.
  • Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle: $\Delta x \cdot \Delta p_x \ge \frac{\hbar}{2}$, where $\hbar = h / (2\pi)$.
  • 1D Time-Independent Schrödinger Equation: $$-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m} \frac{d^2 \psi}{dx^2} + V(x) \psi = E \psi$$
  • Particle in a 1D Infinite Potential Well (Length $L$): Energy eigenvalues $E_n = \frac{n^2 \pi^2 \hbar^2}{2 m L^2} = \frac{n^2 h^2}{8 m L^2}$ ($n=1,2,3$). Normalized wavefunctions $\psi_n(x) = \sqrt{\frac{2}{L}} \sin\left(\frac{n \pi x}{L}\right)$.
Module 2.detailed_notes:
Module 2 Reference: Quantum Mechanics

Born's statistical interpretation: Probability density of finding particle at $x$ is $P(x) = |\psi(x)|^2$. Total probability $\int_{-\infty}^\infty |\psi|^2 dx = 1$.
Module 2.textbook_html:
2.1 Wave-Particle Duality and Schrödinger Formulation

Microscopic electron transport in semiconductors and quantum dots is governed by wavefunctions satisfying Schrödinger's wave equation.

Module 3.title: Lasers and Fiber Optics
Module 3.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Lasers & Fiber Optics
  • Einstein's Coefficients: $A_{21}$ (spontaneous emission), $B_{12}$ (absorption), $B_{21}$ (stimulated emission). Relation: $B_{12} = B_{21}$, $\frac{A_{21}}{B_{21}} = \frac{8\pi h \nu^3}{c^3}$.
  • Population Inversion: $N_2 > N_1$ achieved via optical/electrical pumping in 3-level or 4-level systems (Nd:YAG, He-Ne, Semiconductor diode).
  • Optical Fiber Numerical Aperture (NA): $$NA = \sin \theta_a = \sqrt{n_1^2 - n_2^2} = n_1 \sqrt{2\Delta}, \quad \Delta = \frac{n_1 - n_2}{n_1}$$
  • Acceptance Angle: $\theta_a = \sin^{-1}(NA)$. Total internal reflection requires core index $n_1 >$ cladding index $n_2$.
Module 3.detailed_notes:
Module 3 Reference: Lasers

Attenuation in optical fibers: Rayleigh scattering ($\propto 1/\lambda^4$), absorption, and modal dispersion.
Module 3.textbook_html:

Module 4.title: Acoustics and Ultrasonics
Module 4.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Acoustics & Ultrasonics
  • Sabine's Reverberation Formula: $T = \frac{0.161 V}{\sum a_i S_i} = \frac{0.161 V}{A}$, where $T$ is reverberation time (decay by $60\,\text{dB}$), $V$ is hall volume ($m^3$), $A$ is total absorption (Sabins).
  • Acoustic Requirements of Good Hall: Optimum reverberation time ($1.0 - 1.5\,\text{s}$ for speech, $1.5 - 2.0\,\text{s}$ for music), Absence of echoes, focusing, resonance, and dead spots.
  • Ultrasonic Production: Magnetostriction generator (up to $100\,\text{kHz}$) and Piezoelectric quartz generator (up to $500\,\text{MHz}$, resonance frequency $f = \frac{p}{2t}\sqrt{Y / \rho}$).
  • Non-Destructive Testing (NDT): Pulse-echo ultrasonic flaw detection locates subsurface voids and weld microcracks without destroying components.
Module 4.detailed_notes:
Module 4 Reference: Acoustics

Acoustic impedance matching: $Z = \rho c$. Reflection coefficient $R = \left(\frac{Z_2 - Z_1}{Z_2 + Z_1}\right)^2$. Coupling gel eliminates air gap during NDT.

Module 5.title: Superconductivity and Magnetic Materials
Module 5.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Superconductivity & Magnetism
  • Meissner Effect: Expulsion of magnetic flux ($B=0$) when cooled below critical temperature $T_c$. Perfect diamagnetism ($\chi = -1$).
  • Critical Magnetic Field: $H_c(T) = H_c(0) \left[ 1 - \left(\frac{T}{T_c}\right)^2 \right]$.
  • Type I vs Type II Superconductors: Type I (complete Meissner up to $H_c$, soft). Type II (vortex mixed state between lower $H_{c1}$ and upper $H_{c2}$, high field superconducting magnets e.g. $Nb_3Sn, YBCO$).
  • Magnetic Classification: Diamagnetic (no permanent dipole), Paramagnetic (unpaired electrons, align with external field), Ferromagnetic (spontaneous domain magnetization, hysteresis loop).
Module 5.detailed_notes:
Module 5 Reference: Superconductivity

BCS Theory: Electron-phonon-electron pairing forming Cooper pairs below $T_c$ with zero electrical resistance.
